native_mechanisms: A single rolling sphere is the sole carried memory (one accumulator state) across the whole ordered pile of input marks, with old state discarded each step.

Each mark is pressed into the sphere and then rolled a fixed, invariant count of tumbles (fixed mixing rounds per input word), the 'crack angle' at each stalk (rotation) becoming the next carried weight — avalanche by whole-state reshaping, no partial-slice update.
Only the final hairline crack in the last stalk is kept as the emitted token; all intermediate cracks, dust and footprints are discarded on purpose (no per-step outputs, no history retained).
core_technique: Off-the-shelf SipHash-2-4 (ARX add-rotate-xor, fixed 2 rounds per 8-byte word into a 4-word keyed state, 4 finalization rounds, XOR-folded 64-bit output), with a generic textbook 8-lane AVX2 / 2-lane scalar parallel-accumulator tree variant for inputs >= 256 bytes whose lane digests are re-fed through the scalar SipHash — i.e. the standard 'fold the whole buffer through one fixed-round accumulator' construction (same family as the FNV-1a/xxHash known way, substituting rotate-add for multiply) plus conventional SIMD striping, which itself contradicts the 'sole carried sphere' seed.
